machine.name: Dr. Dude And His Excellent Ray

mechanisms.behavior: Three balls rest in the front trough on 11 (right/feed), 12 (middle), 13 (left). Drain contact 10 precedes the outhole coil 1 transfer into the left side of the trough; gravity advances balls toward 11. Coil 2 feeds the rightmost ball into the manual shooter lane 9. Establish three occupied trough contacts at startup and clear each as its ball leaves; do not make coil 1 directly actuate a trough sensor. The table pulses 10 and moves immediately into its virtual stack, which simplifies transit. A persistently occupied outhole/trough or missing feed is ball-search/jam evidence; no dedicated feed-success switch exists beyond 9.
mechanisms.label: Three-ball trough and outhole

mechanisms.behavior: A manual spring plunger launches from shooter lane 9 up the right outer loop toward the rear I Test target 49 and bumper area. Failed/weak shots roll back and keep or reclose 9; a sufficiently strong ball opens 9 and passes the right-loop switch 59. There is no factory autoplunge coil. Public 49 is the emulator simulator shooter slot, not physical hardware.
mechanisms.label: Manual shooter

mechanisms.behavior: The top-left Excellent Ray/Bag of Tricks saucer holds a ball on switch 51. Coil 3 drives the vertical popper AE-24-900 to its overhead habitrail, returning to the left inlane. Rest is spring-return down; clear occupancy only when the ball leaves. The retained table gates eject animation on 51 and clears it at timer step 7; this is visual timing, not a measured kick delay. A trapped ball keeps 51 active and can provoke retries/ball search; there is no extra popper limit switch.
mechanisms.label: Top left popper

mechanisms.behavior: The middle-right Gift of Gab saucer holds switch 32. Coil 4 drives its spring-return vertical popper to the overhead habitrail which returns to the right inlane. The table starts the lift animation whenever 4 fires and clears 32 at timer step 7; ball detection occurs separately. Retain real occupied state until the ball exits. There is no additional position sensor; a ball stuck at 32 is the available jam evidence.
mechanisms.label: Middle right popper

mechanisms.behavior: Four right drop targets 21 (top), 22, 23, 24 (bottom) latch down on hits, detected by the four-bank opto board. Coil 7 lifts/resets the bank and releases the active target states; normal initial state is all up/inactive. A target stuck down remains active and the ROM may retry resets. The retained table also models simultaneous neighboring drops and clears all on ResetDrops. Do not turn each target into a momentary switch or invent a separate reset-complete sensor.
mechanisms.label: Four-target drop bank

mechanisms.behavior: The Magnetic Personality lane has standup 50 near its top and a separate field coil 13 below it. Balls crossing RMagnet are subject to the field only while 13 is active; target 50 is not a magnet-presence opto and output 13 must not write it. The field can hold/release a ball and the lane rolls back toward the left flipper. The assembly has no home sensor or powered mechanical position.
mechanisms.label: Magnet

mechanisms.behavior: The left ramp passes switches 15 then 16 and delivers a ball to the elevated fixed mini-playfield. Motor 16 drives D-13793 gear/post inside its clear shroud, scattering the ball into nine standups: Gab 33-35 on the right, Heart 36-38 across the rear, Magnet 41-43 on the left. The ball exits the open front onto the right-return habitrail. The motor is on while 16 is active and coasts off; no home/position feedback or absolute orientation is specified. Keep the nine sensors independent, not one synthetic hit sequence. The table SpinUp and SpinDown values of 50 and visual post motion are tuning. Its three #44 matrix lamps 33-35 are distinct from the two flashbulbs per circuit 25-27. Check a jam against ramp, gear/post, target, and motor behavior; no home sensor exists to synthesize.
mechanisms.label: Molecular Mixmaster

mechanisms.behavior: Output 14 pulls the plunger/link and crank of the spring-return Big Shot character; AE-26-1500 on B-11203-R-1 is the assembly-specific coil. Switch 31 is the standup ball target, not a home or character-position sensor. No limit feedback is documented. The table animates an initial rocking sequence then a damped shake; its 20 ms stages are author tuning, not measured machine timings. A jam has no dedicated sensor for the ROM to diagnose.
mechanisms.label: Big Shot
